messages:
alex: Heads up — saw a customer report where tokens appear to be billed twice when a tool_call is invoked mid-stream and the router performs a model downgrade/fallback. Observed with streaming + tool_call + canary fallback.

meera: Repro steps? can you paste request + trace id?

alex: Paste of simplified request payload (redacted):
```json
{
  "model": "redwood-large-v2",
  "stream": true,
  "tool_call": { "name": "search", "args": {} },
  "route_policy": { "fallbacks": ["redwood-medium-quant"] }
}
```
Client trace id: trace-zzz-123. Ledger shows provisional charge for redwood-large-v2 tokens, then confirmed charge for redwood-medium-quant tokens for the same session window. Net result: customer saw both entries in billing telemetry.

jonathan: Is it double-charge or provisional artifact? do we dedupe later?

alex: Looks like ledger writes two line items. We do some provisional -> confirmed reconciliation, but the way we stitch prefixes when fallback occurs means both segments got attributed separately instead of migrating provisional to confirmed.

sara: Right — current stitch logic treats a mid-request fallback like two sessions: prefix from original model, remainder on fallback. For tool_calls we break the stream to invoke the tool and resume; that break seems to be where the router is allowed to swap model.

mike: Is the session id preserved across the tool_call? if not, ledger thinks they're distinct and bills both.

alex: Session id was preserved, but route metadata changes (model_tag) and the ledger attribution key includes model_tag in the current design. So we end up with two keys: (session, modelA) and (session, modelB).

meera: Quick proposals: 1) Prevent router from swapping models mid-stream if `tool_call` is present (strict affinity), OR 2) Change ledger to unify provisional entries across model swaps (migrate provisional from old model to new), OR 3) Console/billing UX: present a single deduped charge and annotate as fallback-merged so customers don't panic.

jonathan: 1 is simplest for correctness but might hurt latency/cost if the fallback was needed for perf. 2 is trickier — we need an idempotent migration path for provisional rows, and guarantees around exactly-once migration. 3 is bandaid but buys time.

sara: For UX we should add a flag on the cost breakdown: `fallback_coalesced: true` and show original tokens, final tokens and net deduped tokens. That should be visible in per-route view + invoice export.

meera: From infra side I'd prefer a hybrid: enforce affinity when `tool_call` present (fast deploy) + start work on provisional migration (longer term). We can canary the affinity guard on a few routes.

alex: Agreed. Action items: I'll draft a tiny RFC for affinity guard + a router flag `prevent_model_swap_midstream_for_toolcalls`. @meera will own tests/canary. @jonathan will design the provisional migration schema and a safe reconcile job. @sara will spec console UI for `fallback_coalesced`. @mike please audit which internal APIs include `model_tag` in ledger key.

mike: Will do. I can grep ledger key usage and open a patch.

ops-bot: started deploy job -> router-affinity-guard/canary-6070003000 (auto)

jonathan: For migration: we should add a tombstone + migrate pattern: mark provisional rows as migrated then create single confirmed aggregate. Need to prove idempotency. I'll sketch it.

sara: UX note: also expose a customer-facing explanation line: "a routing fallback occurred during your request; we consolidated token accounting to avoid double billing" — lets product review wording.

alex: Thanks all. Quick test-plan: reproduce locally with long streaming prompt + tool_call, force router to fallback, observe ledger keys, then try canary with affinity guard. Post results here.

meera: I can reproduce locally within 30m and will post logs.

mike: +1 on affinity guard for now.

jonathan: I'll start a dev doc for migration design.

sara: I'll mock console mockups and link in a follow-up.

alex: sgtm :thumbsup:

meera: on it.
